messages.subject: Missing data in multinomial distribution
parts:
Hi -- I'm new to NIMBLE, so I apologize for these likely basic questions. I'm trying to figure out the best way to handle missing observations in a multinomial distribution of invasive species removal count data. 

I have an array of count data indexed by time, removal observation, and site (y[t,j,i]), and there are inconsistent numbers of removal observations from each site at each time point (missing count data marked as NA in the array). There are two removal methods, denoted "m" and "f". I want these count data to be drawn from a multinomial distribution, where the cell probabilities are the probability of being captured by each removal method (p_m and p_f), conditional upon the probability of being captured at all. For example, if y[t,j,i] was captured with removal type m, the conditional probability would be:
pi_c[t,j,i] = p_m / (total_m_obs[t,i]*p_m + total_f_obs[t,i]*p_f)

And then if y[t,j,i] = NA, then pi_c[t,j,i] = NA.

Here is the code I have been trying:

constants <- list(nsite = dim(DH2020_all_count)[3], #scalar, number of sites, i
                  ntime = dim(DH2020_all_count)[1], #scalar, max number of time periods, t
                  nobs = dim(DH2020_all_count)[2], #scalar, max number of removal observations, j
                  no_f = no_f, #matrix w/ dimensions [t,i] of number of removal observations, type f
                  no_m = no_m, #matrix w/ dimensions [t,i] of number of removal observations, type m
                  obs_ref = DH2020_all_trap_ref) #array [t,j,i] indexing the type of removal observation ("M", "F", or NA for missing)

data <- list(n_cap = n_cap, #matrix w/ dimensions [t,i] total count removed
             y = DH2020_all_count) #array w/ dimensions [t,j,i] for count removed, contains NAs

#write function for calculating conditional probabilities with missing data
calc_cond_prob <- nimbleFunction(
  #input and output types
  run = function(nsite = integer(0), # scalar
                 ntime = integer(0), # scalar
                 nobs = integer(0), # scalar
                 obs_ref = integer(3),  # array
                 p_m = double(0), #scalar
                 p_f = double(0), # scalar
                 no_m = integer(2), # matrix
                 no_f = integer(2)) #matrix
    {
    returnType(double(3))  # array return
   
    # Conditional multinomial cell probabilities
    for(i in 1:nsite){
      for(t in 1:ntime){
        for(j in 1:nobs){
          pic_trap[t,j,i] <- if(is.na(obs_ref[t,j,i])){
            NA
            } else if(obs_ref[t,j,i]=='M'){
            p_m / (no_m[t,i]*p_m+no_f[t,i]*p_f)
            } else if(obs_ref[t,j,i]=='F'){
              p_f / (no_m[t,i]*p_m+no_f[t,i]*p_f)
            }
        }
        }
    }
    return(pic_trap)
  }
)

# Write model code -- removal
removal_code <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Prior distributions
  p_m ~ dunif(0,20) #removal method, m, probability of capture
  p_f ~ dunif(0,20) # removal method, f,  probability of capture
 
  for(i in 1:nsite){
    for(t in 1:ntime){
       
    # Calculate conditional multinomial cell probabilities
    pic_trap[1:ntime,1:nobs,1:nsite] <- calc_cond_prob(nsite,ntime,nobs,obs_ref,p_m,p_f,no_m,no_f)
   
    # multinomial distribution -- observed sample size
    y[t,1:nobs,i] ~ dmulti(pic_trap[t,1:nobs,i], n_cap[t,i])
   
    }
  }
})
   
#build the model
model <- nimbleModel(removal_code,constants,data)

I then get the following error:
Defining model Error in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : 
Error, hit end In addition: Warning messages: 
1: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : NAs introduced by coercion 
2: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : Code obs_ref was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar. This is probably not what you want. 
3: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : Code no_m was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar. This is probably not what you want. 
4: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : Code no_f was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar. This is probably not what you want.

I assume I am doing the Nimble function incorrectly. Also, this brings up the more conceptual question of whether the multinomial distribution can handle NA in the cell probabilities?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Missing data in multinomial distribution
parts:
hi Abigail,

I haven't looked closely at this, but the first thing to modify is that the obs_ref, no_m, nad no_f inputs to calc_cond_prob in your model declaration are vectors and need to be given as such (i.e., with brackets), such as: 

pic_trap[1:ntime,1:nobs,1:nsite] <- calc_cond_prob(nsite,ntime,nobs,obs_ref[1:X,1:Y,1:Z],p_m,p_f,no_m[1:W,1:U],no_f[1:T,1:S])

where you'll need to change 1:X, 1:Y, ..., 1:S, to be the right values for your context. 

The warning messages are trying to say this (by indicating that obs_ref is a scalar in the model but provided as a non-scalar to the model), but they are a bit hard to decipher. 

Also, all model variables are treated internally as doubles (i.e., double precision floating point), so you'll want to have the arguments for your nimble function be double rather than integer. This won't be a problem, since it's fine to store integer-valued numbers as doubles.

The main issue, though, is that I don't think having NAs in your multinomial obs vector will work - it will produce an NA in your likelihood. This will probably be a larger discussion and others may weigh in. One option may be to set up the multinomial as a set of sequential binomials (also called stick-breaking) and impute the missing values in the MCMC. Another would be to use some trickery with nimbleFunctions to sample the missing elements of the multinomial but that would probably take some work. I'm not fully seeing what different possible y vectors you can have... e.g., if you have a single NA, then you actually know that value because the elements have to sum to the multinomial total. 

-chris

Hi Chris,

Thanks so much for your help, and I apologize for my delayed response. 

I have a quick clarification and another question. Previously I mentioned that I have "missing data", but this characteristic of my data is probably better described as a "ragged array" (i.e. NAs in the data represent unequal sample sizes across sites and time points, rather than true missing data). Regarding your comment about NAs in the multinomial, my plan is to fill both the data (y[t,j,i]) and multinomial cell probability vector (pic_trap[t,j,i]) with 0s where there is no data (i.e. edges of the ragged array). Also, per the nimble manual (thanks!), another update I made was to make the array in the is.na() operation in the nimblefunction all numeric values. Previously they were characters.

Ok, so now when I build the model with nimbleModel(), it seems that I have no errors. However, when I try to compileNimble() with the built model, I get the following error:
Error in code$args[[i]]$isCall : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

I'm not sure what the error is referring to?

I've attached a reproducible version of my code. Hopefully it's not too difficult to interpret!

Best,
Abby

messages.subject: Re: Missing data in multinomial distribution
parts:
Hi Abby,

I took a look at this. I also was confused by the error message but this syntax in your nimblefunction calc_cond_prob caught my eye:

          array[t,j,i] <- if(is.na(obs_ref[t,j,i])){ .......

I tried changing the contents of the nimbleFunction to do the assignment inside the if-statements and it seems to work now. I'm pasting the full nimbleFunction below. I have a feeling that in base-R the syntax x <- if(cond) {} is doing something fancy that NIMBLE doesn't support.

Hope this solves the problem--
Ben

calc_cond_prob <- nimbleFunction(
  #input and output types

run = function(nsite = double(0), # scalar
                 ntime = double(0), # scalar
                 nobs = double(0), # scalar
                 obs_ref = double(3),  # array

p_m = double(0), #scalar
                 p_f = double(0), # scalar

no_m = double(2), # matrix
                 no_f = double(2)) #matrix
  {
    returnType(double(3))  # array return
   
    # Conditional multinomial cell probabilities -- trap level
    #create empty array
    array <- array(NA,dim=c(ntime,nobs,nsite))
    #loop through sites, visits, observations

for(i in 1:nsite){
      for(t in 1:ntime){
        for(j in 1:nobs){

array[t,j,i] <- if(is.na(obs_ref[t,j,i])){
            0
          } else if(obs_ref[t,j,i]==2){ #removal type m
p_m / (no_m[t,i]*p_m+no_f[t,i]*p_f)
} else if(obs_ref[t,j,i]==1){ #removal type f

p_f / (no_m[t,i]*p_m+no_f[t,i]*p_f)
          }
        }
      }
    }

return(array[1:ntime,1:nobs,1:nsite])
  }
)

On Friday, January 13, 2023 at 4:18:30 PM UTC-8 Christopher Paciorek wrote:
hi Abigail,

I haven't looked closely at this, but the first thing to modify is that the obs_ref, no_m, nad no_f inputs to calc_cond_prob in your model declaration are vectors and need to be given as such (i.e., with brackets), such as: 

pic_trap[1:ntime,1:nobs,1:nsite] <- calc_cond_prob(nsite,ntime,nobs,obs_ref[1:X,1:Y,1:Z],p_m,p_f,no_m[1:W,1:U],no_f[1:T,1:S])

where you'll need to change 1:X, 1:Y, ..., 1:S, to be the right values for your context. 

The warning messages are trying to say this (by indicating that obs_ref is a scalar in the model but provided as a non-scalar to the model), but they are a bit hard to decipher. 

Also, all model variables are treated internally as doubles (i.e., double precision floating point), so you'll want to have the arguments for your nimble function be double rather than integer. This won't be a problem, since it's fine to store integer-valued numbers as doubles.

The main issue, though, is that I don't think having NAs in your multinomial obs vector will work - it will produce an NA in your likelihood. This will probably be a larger discussion and others may weigh in. One option may be to set up the multinomial as a set of sequential binomials (also called stick-breaking) and impute the missing values in the MCMC. Another would be to use some trickery with nimbleFunctions to sample the missing elements of the multinomial but that would probably take some work. I'm not fully seeing what different possible y vectors you can have... e.g., if you have a single NA, then you actually know that value because the elements have to sum to the multinomial total. 

-chris
